sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog's source for the Bomboli/Bozaba subclassification; contains Bozaba and Bomboli wordlists (possibly tone-marked) and would show whether SIL noted anything prosodic. Likely a lexicostatistic survey silent on stress, but it is the most recent primary data.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale. Études Aequatoria 8. Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria. 284 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Bomboli/Bozaba: the book has 14 sketches (Ebuku, Lifonga, Likata, Libobi, Lobala, Zamba, Baloi, Mbonji, Kunda, Babale, Motembo, Litoka, Balobo, Ndobo) and none is Bomboli or Bozaba. The separator page before p. 89 reads 'SOUS GROUPE LIKOKA: 1. Likoka 2. Bomboli 3. Lobala'; p. 89 names Bomboli as a groupement of Dongo collectivité and as the Lobala's eastern neighbour ('A l'Est, les Likoka et les Bomboli'). The Lobala phonology (p. 91) says only 'La langue atteste deux tons de base (haut et bas); mais elle est déplacée dans beaucoup de mots et flottante dans plusieurs contextes'. N…

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1989. Sur les parlers riverains de la Ngiri. Annales Aequatoria 10: 281-283; and Explorations linguistiques dans la Ngiri, Annales Aequatoria 10: 353-357.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification note: Bomboli is listed among Hulstaert's 'idiomes de la Ngiri' and Lobálá-Likoká-Ngili as a 'terrien' subgroup; mentions de Boeck's tonology-based classification. The second piece is a fieldwork diary (Kungu, Mankanza) listing the parlers recorded (not Bomboli or Bozaba).

sources.citation: de Boeck, L. B. 1951. La tonologie des parlers bantous du nord-ouest du Congo belge. Bulletin des séances de l'Institut Royal Colonial Belge 22(4): 900-919.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tone only. Five areal tonology types; type B 'Bangála-des-marais' = Lingala-type tones shifted one syllable to the right ('tonologie déplacée'), ascribed (pp. 903-904) to all non-riverine populations of the triangle Dongo–Mongala mouth–Ngiri mouth, i.e. the area of Bomboli and Bozaba, but neither name occurs (examples are from Sombe/Bamwe). Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: de Boeck, L. B. 1949. Dialectgroepen in het Ngiri-gebied. Aequatoria 12: 89-94.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Dialect-boundary bundles (42) and a map of 23 dialect groups; group 't' = 'Secteur der Budzaba, Bomboli-hoofdij' corresponding to groups 21 and 18 of the 1948 paper. No linguistic data.

sources.citation: de Boeck, L. B. 1948. Les classifications des langues en Afrique. Bulletin des séances de l'Institut Royal Colonial Belge 19(4): 846-873 (with notes by van Bulck 874-882).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. pp. 865-867: group n° 18 Bomboli (10 villages, 1,340 inhabitants, secteur Lobala-Bomboli, territoire Bomboma; called 'Ngiri' by the Tanda/Likoka) and n° 21 Budjaba (c. 2,400 inhabitants, chefferie des Budjaba; called 'Maleke' by the Bomboli). Ethnonyms, exonyms and populations only.
